lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: comparing two treatments and evaluating published reports
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: comparing two treatments and evaluating published reports

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: n = 400, sample proportion 55%. Margin and interval?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: In 500 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 21 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 4.2% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 4.2% of simulations, which is not unusual.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 85 and standard deviation 3. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 82 and 88?
choices: about 95%
about 68%
about 99.7%
about 50%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.

items.prompt: A random sample of 400 people gives a sample proportion of 65%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±10%, giving 55% to 75%
±5%, giving 60% to 70%
±65%, giving 0% to 130%

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 4 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 4% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 4% of simulations, which is not unusual.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 192 and standard deviation 5. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 187 and 197?
choices: about 68%
about 50%
about 99.7%
about 95%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 57%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±20%, giving 37% to 77%
±57%, giving 0% to 114%
±10%, giving 47% to 67%
±1%, giving 56% to 58%

The simulation proves that there is no difference.
